gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-imperial-ara: Loud and sprawling, Paprika spreads its letters out wide, while Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic keeps its c ends pointing apart like open pincers. The sans-serif text moves along easily.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-inscriptiona: Big, brash, and spaced far apart: that's Paprika up top. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian below it has wide-eyed e and a shapes and a deep middle band, so a long passage goes down smoothly.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-jp: Paprika swaggers in with lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals, a loud and expressive heading. Noto Sans JP answers with a very tall x-height and curves that sweep open, and that lift is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Paprika commands the top with letters scattered at a distance. Noto Sans Kaithi, a plain sans, matches that fullness with lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals, and that shared heft is what ties them together.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Wide-set and bold, with counters like a hollow reed. If Paprika were shrunk down, it would lose its nerve, while Noto Sans Kannada, a plain sans, has gentle bumps up to its capitals and s curves that open wide.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Lowercase that fills the line like capitals is the first thing Paprika shows, with its letters scattered at a distance. Noto Sans Kayah Li has brush ends lifted away before each curve closes.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Paprika is a commanding display face, its hollow-reed counters best kept big and brief. Noto Sans Kharoshthi, a sans with curves that never close back on themselves, lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads clean and modern, its small letters standing proud, almost capital-sized. Paprika is the one to shout with its scattered, expressive letters, while the body font quietly opens generous notches like chisel cuts in wood.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Paprika is commanding and wide, its letters scattered at a distance. Noto Sans Khojki, a sans with a clear, large eye on every e and exits wide enough to pass light through, sits beneath it and keeps the page open.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals make Paprika unmistakable. Noto Sans Khudawadi, a plain sans, keeps capitals and body close in height with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook, so a long passage flows lightly.
